adversarial_audit.objection: Binary transcript indistinguishability does not bound hidden-label recovery.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The MRS proof is fixed-hidden: summing the TV expectation bound over labels yields equation (2). An averaged binary bound alone would not suffice.

adversarial_audit.objection: Covariance can make the averaged PGM output uniform, so no separation follows.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The separation uses correlation between each fixed hidden label and the output, not the unconditioned output marginal.

adversarial_audit.objection: The PGM uses too many copies for the MRS theorem.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Theta(n log n)=exp(o(sqrt(n))), below every fixed positive exp(a sqrt(n)) threshold eventually.

adversarial_audit.objection: Information-theoretic PGM escape supplies an efficient circuit.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False. It only removes a necessity gate; the complete orientation polar remains the implementation bottleneck.

adversarial_audit.objection: Escaping the MRS class proves a quantum speedup.
adversarial_audit.resolution: False. MRS is one restricted quantum model, and no classical complexity lower bound follows from leaving it.

adversarial_audit.objection: The primary theorem's printed success wording is enough without checking its proof.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The argument relies on the proof's explicit transcript-TV conclusion, avoiding the theorem statement's ambiguous use of success probability.

claim_gate.reason: The target PGM is asymptotically outside the entire adaptive MRS transcript class, but no complete orientation-polar circuit or classical hardness theorem is known.

falsifiers_triggered: The explicit fixed-policy transcript zonotope is not a prerequisite for asymptotic target-PGM model escape.
Averaged output uniformity does not erase fixed-hidden label correlation.
MRS escape is already a property of the target measurement, not evidence that its circuit is compiled.
Leaving the MRS class does not establish classical hardness or a quantum speedup.

primary_literature.authors: Cristopher Moore; Alexander Russell; Piotr Sniady
primary_literature.title: On the impossibility of a quantum sieve algorithm for graph isomorphism: unconditional results
primary_literature.used_result: Section 3 sieve definition and Theorem 10 proof: arbitrary adaptive pair selection, fewer than exp(a sqrt(n)) coset states, and exponentially small fixed-hidden transcript TV

proof_obligations.resolution: Fixed-hidden transcript TV transfers to the label-decoding bound 1/n!+exp(-b sqrt(n)), contradicting constant PGM success.
Resolved negatively as a prerequisite. The all-policy identification contradiction already proves target-POVM escape.
The model-class separation supplies no implementation of the restricted child routers, endpoint mixers, or full polar.
The primary theorem leaves its positive character-bound constants and sufficiently-large-n threshold nonexplicit.
Leaving one restricted quantum sieve class does not lower-bound classical graph isomorphism or code equivalence.

summary: Converted the MRS fixed-hidden transcript-TV theorem into an all-policy hidden-label identification bound, proving that the constant-success target PGM is outside the sieve class without a separate transcript-zonotope construction.

theorem.decoder_transfer: uniform-prior transcript identification success is at most 1/M + M^-1 sum_s TV(P_s,P_0)
theorem.fixed_hidden_tv_hypothesis: for every legal hidden flip s, TV(P_s,P_0)<=exp(-b sqrt(n)) when the sieve uses fewer than exp(a sqrt(n)) coset states
theorem.nonclaim: no orientation-polar circuit, explicit MRS constants or finite-n crossover, arbitrary-quantum lower bound, classical hardness, or speedup follows
theorem.pgm_success: the physical hidden-bridge PGM has success at least 4/5 at K=ceil(log2(n!))+2 copies

theorem.source_scope: adaptive pair selection from the entire classical history, weak Fourier sampling at leaves, isotypic sampling after every merge, and final classical transcript postprocessing
